newsitem.title: USA: Chicago council approves $67 mln residential plan.
newsitem.headline: Chicago council approves $67 mln residential plan.

text.p: Chicago's City Council approved a $67 million plan for a condominium and town home development near downtown by CMC Heartland Partners, the Chicago-based real estate partnership announced Wednesday.
The 381-unit mid-rise and high-rise development plan approved earlier this month is CMC's largest to date, the subsidiary of Heartland Partners LP said.
Prices for the units are expected to range from $99,900 to $289,000. The development will be located in a fast-growing area just northwest of the Chicago Loop.

"This is the most prudent and efficient use of the land in today's real estate market," CMC President Ed Jacobson said. "In addition, the Fulton River District's recent residential rebirth and renewed stability make it an attractive and exciting site."
The "Kinzie Station" development will be designed by Pappageorge Haymes Ltd and Smith and Smith Associates, constructed in three phases and marketed to middle and upper-middle income professionals.
